title: Establish canonical installation, deployment, MCP, source, and release references
description:
Every supported binary, deterministic-source, deployment, package, compatibility, upgrade, and MSRV workflow has one maintained adopter-facing home before source freeze.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: INSTALL.md owns supported native and extracted-source-archive installation plus checksum/provenance verification; docs/how-to/deployment.md owns the one-image /repo deployment; a created or existing canonical MCP guide owns package installation/client startup; the release-policy reference owns version, compatibility, upgrade, artifact, source-exclusion, and MSRV procedures.
- [hard] REQ-02: Every command, artifact name, package channel, image tag, mount path, health URL, runtime prerequisite, and version policy in those homes is exercised by automation or explicitly derived from a maintained manifest/workflow source.
- [hard] REQ-03: The canonical pages distinguish supported release paths from contributor source-checkout workflows and contain no instruction that requires an unshipped source-only asset.
- [hard] REQ-04: Link, command-snippet, support-matrix, and source-archive manifest/exclusion checks fail when a canonical path is missing, stale, duplicated, or requires Git metadata absent from the published archive.
- [hard] REQ-05: Completion records that these documents are source-changing freeze inputs; no candidate tag, candidate artifact, or public v1 identity exists, and every later execution leaf consumes the frozen copies without editing prose.

## Notes

Blast radius: `INSTALL.md`, `docs/how-to/deployment.md`, the canonical MCP integration page (created if absent), one release-policy reference, navigation, and doc checks; historical/unrelated conceptual docs are unchanged.
